overall_summary: The performance data is extremely small (max 20 views across all videos), resulting in low statistical confidence. However, early signals show that direct object-based triggers related to communication (phones, names, chats) slightly outperform abstract concepts like late-night thoughts.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos referencing phone names and numbers (A_eLARoegnw with 20 views, aUuNKfe7jm4) performed relatively better than abstract hooks.
winning_patterns.action: Incorporate tangible everyday communication artifacts like contact lists, online status, or typing indicators.

weak_patterns.evidence: Hooks like 'रात के दो बजे' (G0gKV1p3ZHc) and 'मेज पर रखी चाय' (uIbMpCjVutQ) had lower engagement and visibility.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid starting with generic time markers or inanimate objects without an immediate human context.

next_video.concept: Watching a chat box show 'online' for hours without a single message being sent, leading to an overthinking spiral.
next_video.opening_direction: Start right after seeing the green online status on a chat that has been dead for months.
next_video.twist_direction: Realize that being online isn't for you anymore, they are just waiting for someone else.
next_video.reason: Targeting the late evening window when overthinking and phone checking peak among lonely users.

experiment: Testing if shifting the hook from phone numbers/names to active chat behavior (online status) improves initial retention.
